newsitem.title: THAILAND: Moody's officials meet Thai finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Moody's officials meet Thai finance minister.

text.p: Officials from Moody's Rating Service, which has put Thailand on watch for a possible credit downgrade, met Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan on Tuesday to review the economic outlook for the country.

A ministry spokesman told reporters that they held wide-ranging talks on fiscal policies as well as the 100 billion baht spending cuts recently announced by the government and its effect on the current account deficit and economic growth.

Amnuay later said his talks with the Moody's representatives were unofficial, but they would have formal discussions with a government panel of economic officials led by deputy central governor Chaiyawat Wibulsawasdi on Thursday
He said the Moody's officials had enquired about government's latest measures to strengthen the ailing finance sector and he had assured them that there were no serious problems in the sector.

The government, in a major shake up of the troubled finance sector, on Monday ordered 10 finance firms to boost their capital and told banks and finance firms to raise provisions for bad debts, mainly to the depressed property sector.
Moody's had said in mid-February that it had placed Thailand's long term sovereign debt under review for a possible downgrade.

The ministry spokesman added that three other key issues that Moody's officials had asked about were the status of the Thai baht, the central bank's interest rate policy and the national policy on exports which have been sluggish.
The baht was under speculative attack late last year and early this year as pressure from the surging dollar squeezed the Thai unit and rumours of devaluation plagued it.
The central bank maintained a high interest rate policy to counter the baht speculators.
On the baht, he said that the ministry had informed the Moody's officials that Thailand firmly maintained a policy of non-devaluation and that its current value was appropriate.
The central bank expected the tight money market to be more stable by the middle of this month and that interest rates were being held high to deter speculation in the baht.

On exports, the spokesman said the Moody's officials had been told that recently sluggish Thai exports were this year expected to grow by seven or eight percent after a 0.2 percent contraction seen in 1995.
The officials would be given a sector by sector appraisal on exports when they met the panel later this week, he added.
